h1: Rocket CTA — AI & SaaS Call to Action Design
tagline: Call to action reference for an AI or SaaS product, captured at 640x468 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Call to action reference for an AI or SaaS product — React and Tailwind CSS, a dark stage, a stats row and #14191E base.
about: Read Rocket CTA as a call-to-action block spec: the values were written down before the page was built. Colour is limited to deep blue #14191E underneath, set in Inter. The reference is built with React and Tailwind CSS, and the layout decisions are stated independently of it. Motion is confined to 300ms transitions. It is the right reference for an AI or SaaS product call-to-action block that has to look deliberate on the first screen.

layout.title: Top row, one action
layout.body: Navigation is a single row with no second level under it. The bar sits over the 640x468 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Values you can check
layout.body: Type and spacing are drawn from one list here: 10px spacing steps and 300ms transitions. A rebuild that hits those numbers looks like the reference without further tuning.

layout.title: Type sets the hierarchy
layout.body: The type is Inter at the top of the scale, with the supporting copy dropped well below it so the hierarchy needs no colour to read. Weights are specified per role, so the hierarchy does not depend on guesswork at build time. The scale is quoted; use it.

layout.title: The nav is deliberately thin
layout.body: If your own page has more sections, group them rather than widening the bar. The reference was captured at 640x468.

motion.title: Sections arrive with scroll
motion.body: Parallax runs while the page is moving, so the composition has a defined resting state. The composition does not depend on the effect firing, so a fast scroll past it costs nothing. Test it with reduced motion on.

motion.title: Timings in milliseconds
motion.body: Transitions are specified at 300ms, which is the timing the controls are held to. One value is reused across the controls, so their timing cannot drift apart.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over deep blue #14191E, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

notes: The timing budget is state feedback rather than page choreography (300ms), so a slower rebuild reads as a different design. The reference was captured at 640x468, and every value quoted on this page comes from the same brief.
Transitions are specified at 300ms, which is the value to keep when the palette changes.
Transitions are specified at 300ms, short enough that the page never feels like it is waiting for an animation.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the call-to-action block
editorial.body: This is what makes the reference reusable: 10px spacing steps and 300ms transitions. Nothing is left to a default, so a substitution that keeps those numbers keeps the composition. Nothing in this call-to-action block depends on a default.

editorial.title: What this call-to-action block gets right
editorial.body: The trade-off is density: this call-to-action block says less on the first screen than a feature-led layout would. What it keeps is the reading order, and navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the background clip do the work a longer page would spread out. Rocket CTA states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: What moves in Rocket CTA
editorial.body: Ambitious motion usually costs the first screen its legibility. This brief keeps 300ms transitions, parallax layers and hover and press states short enough that the type never has to wait. Nothing animates for its own sake in this call-to-action block.

faq.question: How long is the prompt behind Rocket CTA?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 11,622 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Is the Rocket CTA brief the same as the prompt I would write?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 11,622-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: Rocket CTA was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

audience: Engineers who need the call-to-action block to survive a slow connection will use 640x468 and the type scale as the weight budget.
